In [[mathematics]], the '''[[classifying space]] <math>\operatorname{BSU}(n)</math>''' '''for the [[special unitary group]]''' <math>\operatorname{SU}(n)</math> is the base space of the [[Universal bundle|universal]] <math>\operatorname{SU}(n)</math> [[principal bundle]] <math>\operatorname{ESU}(n)\rightarrow\operatorname{BSU}(n)</math>. This means that <math>\operatorname{SU}(n)</math> principal bundles over a [[CW complex]] up to isomorphism are in bijection with [[homotopy]] classes of its [[Continuous function|continuous]] maps into <math>\operatorname{BSU}(n)</math>. The isomorphism is given by [[Pullback bundle|pullback]]. A particular application are [[Principal SU(2)-bundle|principal SU(2)-bundles]].

== Definition ==
There is a canonical inclusion of complex oriented Grassmannians given by <math>\widetilde\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb{C}^k)\hookrightarrow\widetilde\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb{C}^{k+1}),
V\mapsto V\times\{0\}</math>. Its colimit is:

<math>\operatorname{BSU}(n)
:=\widetilde\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb{C}^\infty)
:=\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}\widetilde\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb{C}^k).</math>

Since real oriented Grassmannians can be expressed as a [[homogeneous space]] by:

: <math>\widetilde\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb{C}^k)
=\operatorname{SU}(n+k)/(\operatorname{SU}(n)\times\operatorname{SU}(k))</math>

the group structure carries over to <math>\operatorname{BSU}(n)</math>.

== Simplest classifying spaces ==

* Since <math>\operatorname{SU}(1)
\cong 1</math> is the [[trivial group]], <math>\operatorname{BSU}(1)
\cong\{*\}</math> is the trivial topological space.

* Since <math>\operatorname{SU}(2)
\cong\operatorname{Sp}(1)</math>, one has <math>\operatorname{BSU}(2)
\cong\operatorname{BSp}(1)
\cong\mathbb{H}P^\infty</math>.

== Classification of principal bundles ==
Given a [[topological space]] <math>X</math> the set of <math>\operatorname{SU}(n)</math> principal bundles on it up to isomorphism is denoted <math>\operatorname{Prin}_{\operatorname{SU}(n)}(X)</math>. If <math>X</math> is a [[CW complex]], then the map:<ref name=":36">{{cite web |access-date=2024-03-14 |language=en |title=universal principal bundle |url=https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/universal+principal+bundle |website=[[nLab]]}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

: <math>[X,\operatorname{BSU}(n)]\rightarrow\operatorname{Prin}_{\operatorname{SU}(n)}(X),
[f]\mapsto f^*\operatorname{ESU}(n)</math>

is [[Bijection|bijective]].

== Cohomology ring ==
The [[cohomology ring]] of <math>\operatorname{BSU}(n)</math> with coefficients in the [[Ring (mathematics)|ring]] <math>\mathbb{Z}</math> of [[Integer|integers]] is generated by the [[Chern class|Chern classes]]:<ref name=":35">Hatcher 02, Example 4D.7.</ref>

: <math>H^*(\operatorname{BSU}(n);\mathbb{Z})
=\mathbb{Z}[c_2,\ldots,c_n].</math>

== Infinite classifying space ==
The canonical inclusions <math>\operatorname{SU}(n)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{SU}(n+1)</math> induce canonical inclusions <math>\operatorname{BSU}(n)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{BSU}(n+1)</math> on their respective classifying spaces. Their respective colimits are denoted as:

: <math>\operatorname{SU}
:=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\operatorname{SU}(n);</math>
: <math>\operatorname{BSU}
:=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\operatorname{BSU}(n).</math>

<math>\operatorname{BSU}</math> is indeed the classifying space of <math>\operatorname{SU}</math>.
